newsitem.title: CANADA: Alberta harvest at three-week standstill on rain.
newsitem.headline: Alberta harvest at three-week standstill on rain.

text.p: Alberta made next to no harvest progress in the last three weeks on rain and up to five inches of snow in the past weekend, Alberta Agriculture said of the week ended September 30.
The harvest was 50 percent complete by September 30, compared with 85 to 90 percent a year ago.
Southern Alberta's harvest was 80 to 90 percent complete.
Central Alberta's harvest remained at 50 percent done. Crops showed severe stress due to cool, wet conditions.
Northeast Alberta remained at 40 percent harvested. Up to five inches of snow fell on the region over the weekend.
Northwest Alberta remained at 15 to 20 percent harvested. Sprouting and head diseases such as alternaria, cladosporium and septoria became prevalent in many fields.
Peace River Valley's Fort Vermillion and Manning districts managed to combine 70 to 75 percent of their crops but the rest of the region stayed at 10 to 15 percent complete.
